attributes.probed_form:
THE SPLIT BOUNDARIES, derived from the dtk split asm and not guessed. gamemain.c extab 0x800061D8..0x80006320 (was ..0x80006388), extabindex 0x80009B14..0x80009D00 (was ..0x80009D9C), .text 0x80050054..0x80055CB8 (was ..0x80058078); gauntworld.c takes the remainder from those addresses. The extabindex cut is at DoWorldAnimation's entry @eti_80009D00 because FindWobjWanim (the block's first .text function) has NO exception entry, and the extab cut at 0x80006320 is the table that entry points to; the last gamemain-block entry is fn_80055AFC's @eti_80009CF4 -> @etb_80006318, and 0x80006318 + 8 = 0x80006320 closes it exactly.

THE THREE INLINE-BOUNDARY REPAIRS, each measured. (a) ActivateSpecialTrigger (0x8005FF60, gauntworld's own, NOT moved) went 100.0000% -> 77.3853% the moment FindWobjWanim's definition entered this TU, because -inline auto folded the callee in. `#pragma dont_inline on` around ActivateSpecialTrigger restores the out-of-line call; the SAME pragma placed around FindWobjWanim instead does NOT work -- it also blocks the static helper worldAnimIndexMatches from being inlined INTO FindWobjWanim and takes that function to 0.0000%, and hand-inlining the helper under the bracket leaves it at 99.5000%. The bracket belongs on the CALLER. (b) With the bracket on, ActivateSpecialTrigger read 99.9083% with a pure frame delta -- ten IMMEDIATE rows, `stwu r1,-80(r1)` target vs `-88` ours, `stmw r22,32(r1)` vs `40`, `addi r1,r1,80` vs `88` -- because the function's `u8 _spare[8]` pad had been sized against the pre-move codegen. Deleting the pad closed it to 100.0000%, and the arbiter for that half is slotdiff, not the IMMEDIATE rows: `python tools/gdl/slotdiff.py game/world/gauntworld ActivateSpecialTrigger` now prints `frame: target 80  ours 80   saves: target r22  ours r22` and `== ActivateSpecialTrigger: target 8 slots, ours 8 -> SLOT MAP IDENTICAL`, with every offset row reading `T n / O n` (-80, 4, 24, 28, 32, 72, 80, 84). (c) fn_80057024 went 92.7182% -> 73.8923% in the OTHER direction: `fndiff --ops` reported 'target 362 insns, ours 292' with two `bl` in ours where the target has two 26-instruction runs of lbz/extsb/extsb/cmpw/bne/lbz/extsb./beq -- InLevel, expanded twice. Emitting the block in TARGET .text ORDER puts InLevel (0x800579E0) after fn_80057024 (0x80057024), and mwcc only inlines a function already defined, so the expansions were lost. Hoisting InLevel's definition above fn_80057024 restored 92.7182% exactly. That is a measured statement about the real TU: its SOURCE order is not its .text order for InLevel.

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: Emit the block in reverse .text order and re-run `python tools/gdl/fuzzy.py game/world/gauntworld`: if fn_80057024 does not hold at or above 92.7182% and the other 23 rows do not hold at their current values, the reversal is wrong and the hoist-what-is-needed form stands. `python tools/gdl/textorder.py game/world/gauntworld` decides the other half -- a reversal that helps inlining but misorders .text is not a win.
hypothesis.count_consequence: count-neutral for every function that neither gains nor loses an inline expansion; for a function that regains one it is T-vs-O convergent (fn_80057024 went 292 -> 362 ours when the expansions came back, against target 362).
hypothesis.screened_against_target: no -- only the InLevel/fn_80057024 pair was measured. The other 23 functions were not checked for cross-inlining in either direction, and textorder was not re-run against a reversed layout.
hypothesis.statement: The gauntworld block's source order is REVERSE .text order, not .text order. The one measured datum is InLevel: the target inlines it twice into fn_80057024, which .text places 0x9BC bytes EARLIER, and mwcc cannot inline a function defined later -- so in the real TU InLevel precedes fn_80057024 in source while following it in .text. Reversing the block would put InLevel, LevelLetter, GetEnemySubtype, GetEnemyTypes and PrintWorldMemSizes ahead of fn_80057024 and world_update, which is exactly the direction the Xbox PDB roster alignment already runs (gauntworld.obj reversed matches the GC block row for row for seven rows).
